neighbours.label: A classifying modifier that names the type of the noun about to follow in a compound (a ⟦float⟧ plane, ten⟦or⟧ saxophone, a portable ⟦Bluetooth⟧ speaker, ⟦duct⟧ insulation); the other pole takes size and openness adjectives (big, large, open)
fire: The plumber wrapped the hallway in pipe insulation before winter.
She plays alto clarinet in the town's wind band.
They crossed the bay in a small cargo ferry.
He ordered a wireless USB keyboard for the office.
The garden has a pretty stone bridge over the stream.
The clinic offers a brow lift under local anaesthetic.
We rented a canal boat for the long weekend.
The lab studies a nuclear hormone receptor found in the liver.
quiet: The plumber wrapped the hallway carefully and left before winter.
She plays loudly and well in the town's wind band.
They crossed the bay slowly and arrived after dark.
He ordered something cheap and simple for the office.
The garden has a stream, and it is very pretty.
The clinic offers advice freely and without an appointment.
We rented it together for the long weekend.
The lab studies how the liver responds when hormones arrive.

notes: Card: no single token; peaks are the first element of noun compounds. The + pole peaks on ' big', ' open', ' large'. Probes: float plane 0.90, Bluetooth speaker 0.72, tenor saxophone 0.69, neck lift 0.29; the same noun as a head ('pain in his neck') 0.01, size adjectives 0.09.
